title: Moon base: the 354-hour night (one night, one place)
note: Nov 23. One base, one event: the Sun leaves, the lamps come on, people work in the dark, the Sun returns, the dark starts back. Same sentences and voice as before. Shots 1 and 4 are NASA's 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026), a 1080x1920 window at 1:1, with the travelling shadow, the night and every lamp added by night_fall.py (specs/night_take1.json, night_take2.json); shot 4 runs the same camera move backwards from where shot 1 ends. Shots 2 and 3 are NASA's 'Moon Base: Rovers and Lunar Terrain Vehicles' (Oct 2026), untouched apart from the 9:16 window. Shot 5 is AI-moved (LTX-2.3) from NASA's rendering 'Moon Base Phase 1'. Credit NASA. Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py); no recordings.

shots.job: This shot shows a base on a sunlit plain as a ridge's shadow crosses it and its lamps come on one by one, so the viewer watches the night arrive. (NASA concept animation; shadow, night and lamps added)
This shot shows an astronaut kneeling at work in dim light, so the viewer sees the people a base cannot switch off. (NASA, Rovers video, 0:18)
This shot shows a glove holding a rock, lit only by helmet lamps, so the viewer feels what working through the night means. (NASA, Rovers video, 0:26)

This shot shows the same base in the dark with its lamps on, then the sunlight coming back and the shadow starting to return, so the viewer sees that light at the pole is long but not permanent. (NASA concept animation; shadow, night and lamps added)
This shot shows two astronauts walking to their rover in sunlight with Earth above the ridge, so the viewer sees what has been promised. (AI-moved from NASA's rendering)

lines.say: A Moon base would face nights about three hundred and fifty-four hours long.

lines.say: Small landers have survived them by mostly shutting down.
No base with people has yet run through a lunar night.
